sections.label: README.md
sections.title: David Fetzer
paras: I build infrastructure — tooling for AI coding agents, map servers, command-line tools, self-hosted platforms, and the hardware underneath them.

Seven independent projects carry this page: a deterministic code map for AI coding agents, a local-first runner for those agents across machines, a self-hosted Mapbox alternative that was acquired in 2026, a static Go binary for browserless file transfer, a private LLM and RAG platform on Kubernetes, a secure element board for the Raspberry Pi, and a 3D-printing service that prices and fulfils uploaded parts.

sections.label: mapwright
sections.title: mapwright
paras: A self-hosted map server. The full Mapbox stack — tiles, styles, geocoding, routing, static maps — running on your own hardware as a single Docker image with embedded Postgres. Founded in June 2026 and acquired the same year.

Mapwright speaks Mapbox and MapTiler URL shapes, so existing MapLibre applications migrate by changing a base URL rather than rewriting against a new SDK. It runs air-gapped for on-premise and data-residency requirements.

rows.label: 01 tiles
rows.body: Vector and raster tiles. 127 GB for full-planet coverage.

rows.label: 02 styles
rows.body: Visual style editor with five standard styles.

rows.label: 03 geocoding
rows.body: Forward and reverse geocoding with POI search.

rows.label: 04 routing
rows.body: Directions, matrix, isochrone, map-matching, optimization. 93 GB, full planet.

rows.label: 05 static maps
rows.body: Server-rendered static maps.

rows.label: 06 wmts/wms
rows.body: WMTS and WMS for standards-based GIS clients.

rows.label: 07 api keys
rows.body: Scopes, origin allowlists, metering, and rate limits.

rows.label: 08 admin
rows.body: Admin console.

rows.label: 09 mcp
rows.body: An MCP server exposing migration, reference, and live-API tools to coding agents, so an assistant can port an app off Mapbox or call a running instance. Admin operations are deliberately excluded from the tool surface.

sections.label: osnova
sections.title: osnova
sections.kicker: deterministic code map for AI coding agents · getosnova.dev
paras: Osnova indexes a repository into a symbol and call graph with tree-sitter, then serves it to any MCP client or from the command line. Same input, same output, byte for byte: no embeddings, no telemetry, and no network connection unless asked.
Twenty languages, seven with deep adapters: TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Go, Rust, Java, and C#. Published on npm as @getdomovoi/osnova under Apache-2.0.

rows.label: tools
rows.body: Ten tools over MCP and the CLI: task context, symbol and text search, callers and callees, change impact from a diff, test discovery, and unreferenced-code candidates.

rows.label: answers
rows.body: Every answer carries exact file and line, the resolution basis of each edge, and an exact count of what its budget left out. An empty caller list reads as no indexed caller, never as proof of none.

rows.label: determinism
rows.body: Two fresh builds of the same tree produce identical index hashes.

rows.label: clients
rows.body: One global install wires Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Kilo, and Pi with MCP entries, hooks, and a shared skill. Setup previews its diff and writes nothing until --apply.

sections.label: domovoi
sections.title: domovoi
sections.kicker: local-first runner for AI coding agents · apache-2.0
paras: A daemon sits beside the code and renders its agent sessions in desktop, browser, and mobile clients. Repository state, credentials, terminals, worktrees, and tool execution stay on the execution machine; clients receive typed state, diffs, terminal streams, approval requests, and sandboxed previews.

rows.label: protocol
rows.body: A versioned Zod protocol over authenticated WebSocket JSON-RPC, covering permissions, sessions, approvals, threads, and artifacts.

rows.label: clients
rows.body: A desktop app on Electron, an installable browser PWA, an Expo mobile app, and a terminal CLI, sharing one React workspace.

rows.label: approvals
rows.body: Ask, Plan, and Build are permission modes. Hard gates require explicit approval, and smaller screens collapse information without omitting approval facts.

rows.label: security
rows.body: Every daemon requires authentication. Remote listeners are opt-in and terminate TLS themselves; a plaintext non-loopback listener is refused. Previews load only with short-lived signed capabilities scoped to one artifact revision.

rows.label: licensing
rows.body: Open-core. The daemon, protocol, clients, and local transports are Apache-2.0.

sections.label: 3dpass
sections.title: 3dpass
paras: A 3D-printing service. A customer uploads a mesh, the server measures it, prices it, takes payment through Stripe, and tracks the part through printing and shipping.
Next.js and Convex, with a Python bridge on the print-farm LAN: the printers have no public ingress, so the bridge connects outbound, mirrors telemetry, and advances jobs.

rows.label: pricing
rows.body: Server-authoritative. The browser posts a print configuration and receives totals — never a coefficient, never a rate.

rows.label: measurement
rows.body: Volume is the billing quantity, so it is recomputed server-side from the stored bytes rather than trusted from the client.

rows.label: boundaries
rows.body: Every backend function declares argument and return validators; money and status writes are internal-only, reachable from the signed Stripe webhook.

rows.label: bridge
rows.body: Ships with a simulator driving the same contract as the printers, so the admin queue and order flow run with no hardware attached.

rows.label: testing
rows.body: Playwright end-to-end and unit tests across the money, authorization, and file paths, with enforced coverage thresholds. CI is the only path to production.

sections.label: transfer-it-cli
sections.title: transfer-it-cli
paras: A single static Go binary for MEGA's transfer.it, shipping as both an interactive TUI and a scriptable CLI. Built for machines without a browser — servers, embedded boxes, SSH-only sessions. Zero runtime dependencies.

rows.label: protocol
rows.body: The upload path is reverse-engineered from transfer.it's WebSocket protocol.

rows.label: throughput
rows.body: Multi-pool parallel connections, in-session retry with exponential backoff, and token-bucket bandwidth limiting over a shared HTTP/2 client with TLS session resumption.

rows.label: memory
rows.body: Transfers stream, so memory stays bounded by the chunk size — under a megabyte, even on 20+ GiB files.

rows.label: resume
rows.body: Uploads, downloads, and recursive folder uploads all resume after process restart, tracked by a per-transfer chunk bitmap with per-chunk MAC verification that stays forward-compatible across binary upgrades.

rows.label: packaging
rows.body: Six cross-compiled targets plus native .deb, .rpm, and .apk packages.

rows.label: ci
rows.body: staticcheck, govulncheck, and race-detector tests across Linux, macOS, and Windows, alongside a weekly check that hashes upstream bundles and opens an issue when the service changes underneath it.

sections.label: ai-platform
sections.title: self-hosted ai platform
sections.kicker: a guarded ops agent over private LLM and RAG infrastructure
paras: A multi-node K3s cluster running across Raspberry Pis, with GPU inference offloaded to a virtualized host elsewhere on the same network. Open WebUI, Ollama, a FastAPI retrieval service over a Qdrant vector store, Prometheus and Grafana observability, and automated backup-freshness checks.

rows.label: ops agent
rows.body: A read-only operations agent answers infrastructure questions from runbooks and from live cluster state, calling tools and parsing their output into typed views rather than pasting raw text back.

rows.label: safety
rows.body: Every request passes a default-deny safety router before any tool or retrieval runs: an LLM intent classifier and a regex gate work independently, and either one flagging write intent stops execution. Writes return a scoped review checklist marked proposed_action_only — the agent drafts, a human applies, and it may never report a change as done.

rows.label: architecture
rows.body: Mixed-architecture throughout. Cluster workloads are arm64 images built and served from a private registry with upstream images pinned by digest, while inference runs on x86 with a passed-through consumer AMD GPU.

rows.label: inference
rows.body: Vulkan rules out flash attention and KV-cache quantization, so throughput comes from context and keep-alive tuning instead.

rows.label: services
rows.body: Python and FastAPI services, a Go backend-for-frontend, React and TypeScript console.
